original_question: More generally, what smoothness can be proved for solutions of initial-boundary value problems for dispersive equations in arbitrary spatial dimension?
target_in_paper: Problem 5 (initial boundary value problems for integrable systems (IBVP)), specifically the broad concluding open problem that follows the NLS/Robin-boundary regularity discussion: to understand what can be said about the smoothness of solutions of IBVPs for dispersive equations in any dimension. ([sigma-journal.com](https://sigma-journal.com/2017/016/sigma17-016.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly captures the paper’s broad open question about smoothness/regularity of solutions to initial-boundary value problems for dispersive equations, and it also correctly preserves the paper’s move from a specific NLS half-line problem to an arbitrary-spatial-dimension formulation. ([sigma-journal.com](https://sigma-journal.com/2017/016/sigma17-016.pdf))
missing_details: The draft does not say that this broader question is introduced only after a more specific open problem for the nonlinear Schrödinger equation on the half-line, so it loses the paper’s motivating prototype. ([sigma-journal.com](https://sigma-journal.com/2017/016/sigma17-016.pdf))

The paper’s concrete setup is NLS on x ≥ 0, t ≥ 0 with determining data u(x,0)=f(x) and u(0,t)=g(t), and then, in the key regularity discussion, Robin boundary condition u_x(0,t)+q u(0,t)=0; this context is absent from the draft. ([sigma-journal.com](https://sigma-journal.com/2017/016/sigma17-016.pdf))

The draft does not include the paper’s only explicit regularity benchmark: for sufficiently smooth compatible data, one expects the solution to be classical on x>0, t>0, meaning C^2 in space and C^1 in time. ([sigma-journal.com](https://sigma-journal.com/2017/016/sigma17-016.pdf))

The draft omits the compatibility or matching requirement at the corner (x,t)=(0,0), which the paper explicitly includes in the classical-regularity expectation. ([sigma-journal.com](https://sigma-journal.com/2017/016/sigma17-016.pdf))

The phrase dispersive equations is left unanchored; in the paper, the broader question is motivated by the failure of standard Sobolev iteration for NLS with Robin data and by the lack of a general PDE regularity theory in that setting. ([sigma-journal.com](https://sigma-journal.com/2017/016/sigma17-016.pdf))

The draft does not indicate that the arbitrary-dimension question is intentionally informal in the paper: no fixed class of dispersive operators, domains, or boundary conditions is specified beyond the motivating NLS example, so any sharpening must remain explicitly tied to that example rather than replace it. ([sigma-journal.com](https://sigma-journal.com/2017/016/sigma17-016.pdf))
refined_question: Motivated by the half-line nonlinear Schrödinger initial-boundary value problem discussed in Problem 5, especially the Robin-boundary case, where for sufficiently smooth initial and boundary data satisfying the necessary compatibility conditions at (0,0) one expects a classical solution (C^2 in the spatial variables and C^1 in time), what can actually be proved in arbitrary spatial dimension about the smoothness of solutions to initial-boundary value problems for dispersive equations?
justification: The draft is very close to the paper’s final broad sentence on this point, but in the paper that sentence is explicitly presented as a generalization of a more concrete NLS regularity problem. Deift first formulates the specific open problem of proving that the half-line NLS IBVP with a general class of nonlinearities, Robin boundary conditions, and matching smooth data is classical on x>0, t>0; only then does he broaden the discussion to dispersive IBVPs in any dimension. The refined question therefore keeps the arbitrary-dimension scope from your draft while restoring the motivating NLS/Robin context and the paper’s only explicit smoothness target, namely classical regularity in the sense C^2 in space and C^1 in time. ([sigma-journal.com](https://sigma-journal.com/2017/016/sigma17-016.pdf))
